title: Nodics as Data as a Service
readerIntent: Evaluate Nodics as a governed business-data platform.
priorKnowledge: Understand APIs, schemas, security, search, import/export, and operations.
owner: Composed Nodics data, API, security, search, import/export, and operational capabilities
summary: Nodics can expose tenant-safe business data through stable APIs, search, imports, exports, events, workflows, and BackOffice while each domain retains ownership.

sections.heading: Business outcomes
items: Centralize governed data definitions without coupling consumers to database providers.
Deliver API and search access to websites, mobile clients, partners, operations, and assistants.
Accelerate new customer applications through reusable schemas, services, routes, permissions, and observability.
Support PIM, content, commerce, logistics, and partner-defined domains through modules.

sections.heading: Adoption path
items: Identify authoritative domains, owners, consumers, tenant/enterprise scopes, service objectives, and regulatory constraints.
Reuse or extend existing schemas before creating new models.
Expose least-privilege versioned APIs and query contracts.
Configure providers, import/export, cache/search, events/workflows, audit, backup, and recovery.
Validate isolation, performance, failure, migration, and operational evidence before production.

sections.heading: Limits
paragraphs: DaaS is a composition of implemented capabilities, not an unrestricted database endpoint. Consumers cannot bypass target authorization, validation, ownership, or provider-neutral service contracts.
